precepts.text: The world is divided into ten parts and ten parts of it are gone already. That was during the time of Ezra; understand we are in the last days and the clock is ticking. Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people. Notice we start first with setting our own houses in order; then we have the ability to tell somebody else to get right. If we are going to set our houses in order, where do we start? With your marriage. If the home front is not right, how are you going to get out there and instruct your people?
precepts.point: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: he sees what is about to happen and he prepares for that. But the simple pass on, and are punished. Somebody watching this class is taking notes, saying that is some good stuff, and then will immediately close their Bible, go home, and proceed to be a demon. You saw the evil, but you are not hiding.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
“A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself”. Knowing the time, we had better prepare ourselves. Ezra was told: “For the world is divided into twelve parts, and the ten parts of it are gone already, and half of a tenth part: And there remaineth that which is after the half of the tenth part.”

That was during the time of Ezra. Understand that we are in the last days; the clock is ticking, brethren. We have leadership able to show us what is going to come to pass, and we just saw Daniel 3 come to life before our eyes. Babylon is going to burn. If you're smart, you'll get ready.

“Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people, comfort such of them as be in trouble, and now renounce corruption”. Knowing the time, we must set our houses in order. Notice we start first with setting our own houses in order; then we have the ability to tell somebody else to get right and fix their stuff.

If we are going to set our houses in order, where do we start? With your marriage; that is the first place. If the home front isn't right, how are you going to get out there and instruct your people? How are we going to inherit what the Lord has prepared for us if we are not taking this Bible seriously? The simple take notes, say that's some good stuff, close the Bible, go home and proceed to be a demon. They saw the evil but they aren't hiding, and they pass on and are punished.

precepts.text: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? He shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men. Business meaning God's business. This is why you see us meeting dignitaries across the world: because we've been diligent in God's business. Mean men are obscure men; stop wasting your time debating obscure people on the internet who only want clout.
precepts.point: The famine was over all the face of the earth, and all countries came into Egypt to Joseph for to buy corn. That's what it's like when you have a plan, a solution. Joseph didn't sit around and wait for the dearth; the Most High showed him what was coming, and he made moves of preparation. This is how we have to be in IUIC.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
“at the end of two full years” Pharaoh dreamed of seven fat kine eaten up by seven lean kine, and seven good ears devoured by seven thin ears “blasted with the east wind.” None of the magicians could interpret it, until the chief butler remembered his faults and told Pharaoh of the young Hebrew. “Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.”

Solomon wrote the precept: “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.” The business is God's business. Joseph was diligent in it in Potiphar's house and in the prison, and now a slave out of the dungeon stands before the king of Egypt. Even there he gave God the glory: “It is not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.”

And he did not come to Pharaoh with only a problem. He told him the dream is one, seven years of plenty and seven of famine, “because the thing is established by God,” and then he told him exactly what to do: appoint officers, take up the fifth part in the plenteous years, and lay up corn against the famine. To every problem, brothers, we must have a solution. Some spirits among us have a problem for every solution; stay away from brothers and sisters like that.

So Pharaoh said, “Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of God is?” He put his ring upon Joseph's hand, arrayed him in fine linen, made him ride in the second chariot, “and they cried before him, Bow the knee.” We are going to tell the nations that too: bow the knee. “Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh”; he went in at 17 and spent 13 years in servitude and prison before he stood before the king.

This is why you see Israel today meeting dignitaries across the world: because we have been diligent in God's business. Mean men are obscure men, bums on the internet with a handful of followers who want to debate you for clout, whose numbers go up as soon as they see the shirt. They are not worth your time. A man diligent in God's business stands before kings.

precepts.text: Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go: lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul. The bitter brother is like that dangerous brush; there could be a viper in there. Get too close and the bitter spirit gets on you.
precepts.point: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners. Bitterness spreads like leaven through words: the yeast makes the thing rise, and the angry influence spreads to others through words and attitude.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
“evil communications corrupt good manners.” Bitterness spreads like leaven through words: the yeast makes things rise, and that is what bitterness does. The root of bitterness corrupts your spirit and messes with your attitude, and that angry influence spreads to others through words and through attitude.

So Proverbs warns: “Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go”. You see that brother is bitter; he is like that dangerous overgrown brush. There could be a viper in there, anything on the other side of that bush. Move.

“Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.” Now that bitter brother has put the bitter spirit on you. You got bit, like Bird Box, and now you are looking dumb. That is the snare right there.

That is why the scripture says be not deceived. Keeping company with the bitter brother is how the leaven gets into you. His evil communications will corrupt your good manners, and his offenses will reach others, starting with the first offense, the one in your own house.

precepts.text: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
precepts.point: If there is no candy or donuts in the house, a six-year-old cannot get them. Do not offer children a choice between sugar and good food; they will always choose sugar.

note.label: My Temple My Choice

precepts.why:
Ezekiel says the proverb will be used against us: “As is the mother, so is her daughter.” Very rarely do you see a fat mother and a skinny daughter. If the mama is big, the daughter is big, and if there is a son, he is really big too, because what you eat to get there is exactly what the kids have in the house to eat. The kid models himself or herself after the parents. If you are in the house working out, your kids will want to do push-ups and pull-ups and be in the gym with you. If you like to lie on the bed eating ice cream, they will lie in the bed eating ice cream with you. That self-hatred gets passed on, and that is how the cycle continues: grandmama's fat, mama's fat, the kid is fat, and they all give the same excuse, my thyroid, we big boned. Garbage.

So Proverbs gives the command: “Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.” It is you that has to shape and mould the trajectory of the kid's life. That goes from teaching them the laws, to showing them what is good to eat and what is not good to eat, to showing them to exercise and to do their studies: train them in the right direction in every aspect.

If there is no candy in the house, can a six-year-old go outside and buy candy? Hell no. If there are no donuts in the house, can a six-year-old go and buy donuts? The kid eats what you feed them. And stop giving your kids choices: put sugary food and good food before a kid and ask what they want, and they will always choose sugar. A kid does not know. When your kid loves a healthy food, give it to them all the time.

If you are big and your kid is big, how will you feel when your young kid needs insulin shots because he is diabetic from being overfed on all kinds of garbage? Where is the love in that? Laziness is why a lot of the time we don't deal with our kids right and we don't deal with ourselves right. If we want to save our kids, it starts with you first: control your eating and exercise, and then you are setting the right example, so that the daughter who is as her mother is trained in the right way.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning. Learn them and apply them.
precepts.point: Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge, that I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth? The Bible is God's excellent things, not a prosperity tool or a debate about what we feel like doing. He expects excellence, so change your mind to his standard instead of the crumbs society leaves our people.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.” The excellent things God wrote in Proverbs 22:20, the counsels and knowledge that make us “know the certainty of the words of truth”, were written for us to learn.

And not only to learn: “that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” These excellent things are written for us to apply to our lives, so that we can be excellent and great in God’s eyes. Learn and apply, that is what Romans 15:4 is telling us.

Everything in this Bible is the excellent things of God, the truth he wants us to know. It is not to be used to get rich off of prosperity teaching, and it is not up for debate for us to decide what we should and should not do. It is not up for debate whether we want to be great or average. God gave us excellent things because he expects excellence out of us.

So we have to change our mindset and live up to the standards of God, not the standards the world has placed on black men and women and Hispanic men, to be comfortable with the crumbs society gives us. Those excellent things are what we have to apply, and it starts with a change in the mind.

precepts.text: Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth, for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed. He wants action, not lip service.
precepts.point: Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge, that I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth? The Bible is God's excellent things, not a prosperity tool or a debate about what we feel like doing. He expects excellence, so change your mind to his standard instead of the crumbs society leaves our people.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.”

Actions are weighed when it comes to the Most High. That is why he gave us the excellent things of Proverbs 22:20: to learn them and apply them, because he wants actions behind those things. Not lip service, but actual action from all of us that he called.

Romans 15:4 says the scriptures were written for our learning; 1 Samuel 2:3 says what he does with that learning. He weighs what we do with it. Proud talk and arrogancy out of the mouth weigh nothing with him, because he is a God of knowledge and knows whether the words are backed by works.

That is the pride of thine heart: to talk big about the things of God and not live them. The one who has been given the excellent things has to put his actions where his mouth is, and keep arrogancy out of it.

precepts.text: Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour. He does not reveal himself to everyone, so if he has shown you who you are, you cannot take it lightly.
precepts.point: Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge, that I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth? The Bible is God's excellent things, not a prosperity tool or a debate about what we feel like doing. He expects excellence, so change your mind to his standard instead of the crumbs society leaves our people.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
“Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour.” He hides himself. That means he is not dealing with everybody. It is not like you just say, hey God, and he turns around. He answers and reveals himself to whom he wants to.

So for you to have even a little understanding of his excellent things, to learn them and apply them to your life, means something. He is the “God of Israel, the Saviour.” If God has revealed himself to you, that you are an Israelite, that you even have a mind to conceive his words and understand them, that means something to God. It means you are worthy enough for him to reveal his words to you, so that you get a chance to know what these excellent things are.

You can’t take that lightly. Far too many people in this world do, and use the Bible for material gain and to feel good on their terms. God doesn’t get down like that. He is a God that hides himself, so if he is letting you know what these words mean, you better take heed to him.

And that is where the humbling comes in. Romans 12:3 follows it: “not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” If he is revealing himself to you when he does not deal with everybody, you better have some humbleness, because that is the King of kings, the omnipotent Most High God. We are Israelites and we have to keep God’s commandments, so don’t think too highly of yourself. Humble down.

precepts.text: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; that prudent spirit was on Joseph.
precepts.point: A prudent man foresees the evil coming and makes preparation so he is not consumed in it; the simple pass on and are punished. There is treasure and oil in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish man spends it up; spending irrationally is a spirit of folly.

note.label: Genesis 41: Pharaoh's Dreams and Joseph's Rise Over Egypt

precepts.why:
“A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.” That prudent spirit was on Joseph. He did not stop at the interpretation; he foresaw the seven years of famine and gave the counsel to prepare for them: let Pharaoh set a discreet and wise man over the land, appoint officers, “and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt in the seven plenteous years”, and lay up corn in the cities, “that the land perish not through the famine.”

A prudent man foresees the evil coming and makes preparation so he is not consumed in it. The simple pass on and are punished. Joseph was wise, understanding and diligent, and that is what the counsel shows.

precepts.text: Train up a child in the way he should go: Gideon is doing exactly what we have to do with our young men, teaching them how to walk in the ways of the Lord.
precepts.point: Gideon tells Jether his firstborn, up, and slay them, but the youth drew not his sword, for he feared, because he was yet a youth. We have all had that moment of getting the nudge from pops and being nervous; the son was young, and that is understandable, but you see Gideon being a father, taking his son to the war and teaching him the ways he must walk.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

precepts.why:
Gideon said to Jether his firstborn, “Up, and slay them. But the youth drew not his sword: for he feared, because he was yet a youth.” We have all had that moment of getting the nudge from pops and being nervous; the son was young, and that is understandable. But look at Gideon being a father, taking his son to the war and teaching him the ways he must walk.

“Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.” Gideon is doing exactly what we have to do with our young men, teaching them how to walk in the ways of the Lord, even bringing them to the battle so they learn it.

precepts.text: Train up a child in the way he should go: your job is the training; the revealing belongs to the Most High.
precepts.point: Do not have your children going into a covenant with Christ that he will judge them for if they break it; the scripture says, for this cause many are weak and sickly among you, and many sleep. You do not know if your kids are going to serve the Lord when they go out on their own, or what kind of lusts are in them that will draw them away into the world when they come of age. It is your job as a parent to train them up and pray they stay in it: kids learn by watching, so let them see you take that covenant over and over again until they are ready, and make them rehearse the righteous acts. When the child comes to the age of reasoning and knows the Lord for himself, and the Lord reveals himself to him, you will know it; do not rush it.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.” Your job is the training; the revealing belongs to the Most High.

“Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, neither was the word of the Lord yet revealed unto him.” Look at that. Samuel had been in the house of the Lord since he was weaned, three or four years old, and he still did not know the Lord. This goes in on those playing church with their children: just because your children come and sit and listen to the teaching does not mean they know the Lord. They are there because you brought them there. They can hear all the words they want, but until the Lord reveals himself to them, they do not know him. What makes your kid so special, greater than Samuel?

You do not know if your kids are going to serve the Lord when they go out on their own, or what kind of lusts are in them that will draw them away into the world when they come of age. It is your job as a parent to train them up and pray they stay in it. Kids learn by watching, so let them see you take that covenant over and over again until they are ready, and make them rehearse the righteous acts. When the child comes to the age of reasoning and knows the Lord for himself, and the Lord reveals himself to him, you will know it. Do not rush it.

precepts.text: The diligent tend to plenteousness while the lazy come to want.
precepts.point: See a man diligent in business; he will stand before kings, not before mean men. To deal among the upper echelon you have to be diligent.

note.label: Proverbs 22: A Good Name and Training Up a Child

precepts.why:
“Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.” To deal among the upper echelon you have to be diligent.

Solomon shows where diligence and laziness each lead: “The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.” The diligent tend to plenteousness while the lazy come to want. Even the thoughts of the diligent man are headed toward plenty.

That plenty is what carries a man before kings instead of mean men. Diligence in business is the way up, and want is where hastiness ends.

precepts.text: The mouth of a strange woman is a deep pit for the man abhorred of the Most High.
precepts.point: A whore is a deep ditch and a strange woman a narrow pit. She lies in wait as for a prey and increases the transgressors among men.

note.label: Proverbs 23: Warnings Against Appetite, Wine, and the Strange Woman

precepts.why:
“For a whore is a deep ditch; and a strange woman is a narrow pit.” She lies in wait as for a prey and increases the transgressors among men.

Solomon said the same a chapter before: “The mouth of strange women is a deep pit: he that is abhorred of the Lord shall fall therein.” The mouth of a strange woman is a deep pit for the man abhorred of the Most High. The deep ditch and the narrow pit are the same pit, and the man who falls in it is the one the Lord abhors.

That is why the father says first, “My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.” The heart given to the father and the eyes on his ways do not fall in that pit.

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them; for they shall go into captivity.” The stranger rises above you and you fall low. “He shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him”. “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies”. Our enemies lend to us. In the hood: pawn shops, payday loans, SNAP, EBT. We're in financial ruins, seduced by rap videos and keeping up with the Joneses, buying all kinds of things without knowing God's laws. We're our worst enemies. Train the child to know the borrower, the lender, and his enemy.

Payday loans trap you in interest. Borrow $300 and pay $1,200 or $1,300; you'll be paying interest for the next thirty years. That's extortion, usury, oppression.

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

precepts.why: “Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.” That financial oppression makes a wise man mad.

note.label: Radicalize The Youth

precepts.why: “The Lord shall send upon thee cursing, vexation, and rebuke, in all that thou settest thine hand unto for to do”. God vexes everything we put our hands to, reminding us we sinned against him; in it we realize our enemy. You can't understand who you are without understanding who your enemy is. Parents and leaders do children a disservice by not equipping them. We're not telling you to harm anyone, but know who they are. How many times do they have to lynch your black behind before you understand they don't care? Churches fool people with slavery was good, you didn't protest, good white people took you—stop. Our young ones know the precepts and aren't fools behind that.

note.label: Proverbs 22: A Good Name and Training Up a Child

note.label: Proverbs 22: A Good Name and Training Up a Child

points: The mouth of a strange woman is a deep pit; he that is abhorred of the Most High falls in.

note.label: Proverbs 22: A Good Name and Training Up a Child

note.label: Proverbs 22: A Good Name and Training Up a Child

note.label: Proverbs 22: A Good Name and Training Up a Child

note.label: Proverbs 22: A Good Name and Training Up a Child

note.label: Proverbs 22: A Good Name and Training Up a Child

points: See a man diligent in business; he will stand before kings, not before mean men. To deal among the upper echelon you have to be diligent.

note.label: Proverbs 22: A Good Name and Training Up a Child

points: “Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.” Train young men in scripture so they retain it and can fight what's coming. They'll want to learn. You make this truth look cool.

Society and church have nothing for them, no social services or after-school centers. Get them off the streets and redirect that energy into God's word. Imagine them understanding they're a god on earth, these nations will go into captivity, and in the end they win.
